name: s5_nla_states_vs_shift
title: The statement shift separates language from structure but does not predict what the NLA states within structure
caption: Each dot is one of 47 rows from exps 12, 13, 18, 19 and 22: x = statement shift through the NLA critic, mean over eight paraphrase pairs (horizontal whisker: min to max); y = share of 320 NLA free readouts (40 items x 8) a judge marked as stating the property (vertical whisker: Wilson 95%, which ignores clustering by item). Every structural row has shift ≤ 0.19, yet table column, call argument and parenthesis are stated at 0.30 to 0.41 with shifts near zero; within structural rows Spearman is 0.28 (20,000-shuffle permutation p = 0.08). Filled = structural rows, open = self-inducing rows (language, caps, tense); (n) = experiment. The 0.30 rule is shown only as withdrawn.

checks.quantity: max paraphrase-mean shift over structural rows

notes: Computed from experiments/28_stmt_curve/results/stmt28_*.json (shift, paraphrase min/max, stated) and rows28.json (type, counter/language flags, n readouts). Record discrepancy: exp 28 RESULTS says the paraphrase range exceeds 0.15 on 5 of 47 rows (language rows and tense); the raw files and stats28.json give 8: exp 18 ij2_lang 0.35, exp 12 ij2_lang 0.24, exp 13 tb_sentcount 0.24, exp 12 bk_quote 0.22, exp 22 call argument 0.19, exp 19 call argument 0.17, exp 12 bk_code 0.17, exp 12 nj3_predpos 0.16. Prediction 1 fails either way. Counts k = round(stated x 320) as in analyze28.py. The exp 19 rows enter only as aggregates (no item text).
